title: Auxiliary Power Unit Mount Heat Shield — Removal

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of the auxiliary power unit mount heat shield from the tail cone compartment, with the cooling period, the distortion record and the standoff handling that applies to the stiffened shield.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the mount heat shield for inspection, for replacement or to get access to the forward mount link.
sections.job_setup_note: The compartment must be cool. Do not start the task within two hours of an auxiliary power unit run; the shield and the exhaust duct stay hot long after the unit has stopped and the compartment has no forced ventilation on the ground. Get the depth gauge, the parts tray and the shield support strap. Two people are needed because the shield is awkward rather than heavy.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: DO NOT ENTER THE COMPARTMENT WITHIN TWO HOURS OF AN AUXILIARY POWER UNIT RUN. THE EXHAUST DUCT AND THE SHIELD STAY HOT AND WILL CAUSE BURNS. 2. Make sure the auxiliary power unit is isolated and the start control is tagged. 3. Open the compartment access and put the safety barriers in position. 4. Record the shield distortion at the three positions given in the fits and clearances table with the depth gauge. 5. Attach the support strap to the shield. 6. Remove the shield fasteners, working from the aft edge forward, and keep them in the parts tray. 7. On aircraft post MOD-168086, disconnect the two standoffs at the mount frame before the last fasteners are removed. 8. CAUTION: DO NOT LEVER THE SHIELD OFF THE STANDOFFS. THE STANDOFF SEAT IN THE MOUNT FRAME IS THIN AND WILL DEFORM. 9. Lower the shield with two people and remove it from the compartment. 10. Examine the exposed area of the forward mount link and record any witness marking. 11. Cover the exhaust duct opening if the compartment will be left open.
sections.close_out: Leave the safety barriers in position and the start control tagged until the installation task is complete. Record the distortion measurements and any witness marking on the forward mount link in the aircraft technical log; these values are needed by the installation task.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; step 7 applies to aircraft post MOD-168086 only

safety_precautions: Do not enter the compartment within two hours of an auxiliary power unit run.
Isolate the auxiliary power unit and tag the start control.
